title: は (topic)
meaning: Marks the topic — "as for X". Pronounced わ.
simpleExplanation: は tells the listener what you are talking about: "As for X, ...". Put it after the thing you want to talk about, then say something about it: 私は学生です "As for me, (I) am a student". It is written with the kana は but pronounced わ. Think of は as pointing a spotlight at the topic, and everything after it is the comment.
whenUsed: In almost every sentence: introducing yourself, describing things, asking about someone. Also to contrast two things: 魚は好きですが、肉は好きじゃありません "Fish, I like; meat, I don't".
formation: 私は〜です ／ これは〜です ／ 今日は〜です

examples.reading: わたしは にほんじんです。
examples.note: 私は = "as for me". The rest of the sentence is about me.

examples.reading: あしたは いそがしいです。
examples.note: Time words like 明日 can be the topic too: "As for tomorrow, (I'm) busy".

examples.ja: 魚は好きですが、肉は好きじゃありません。
examples.reading: さかなは すきですが、にくは すきじゃありません。
examples.en: I like fish, but I don't like meat.
examples.note: Two は in one sentence show contrast: fish vs meat.

examples.ja: この店はコーヒーがおいしいです。
examples.reading: この みせは コーヒーが おいしいです。
examples.en: At this shop, the coffee is good.
examples.note: Topic は + subject が: "as for this shop, coffee is good".

examples.ja: 田中さんは今日来ません。
examples.reading: たなかさんは きょう きません。
examples.en: Mr Tanaka is not coming today.
examples.note: The person we are talking about takes は; the verb comes last.

similarGrammar.difference: が marks the subject and often new information or the answer to "who / which". は marks what is already known and being talked about.
も replaces は to say "also": 私も学生です.
Topic and subject in one sentence: 象は鼻が長い.

commonMistakes.why: Question words (誰, 何, どれ) are never followed by は; they take が.
The topic particle is always written は even though it is pronounced わ.

commonMistakes.wrong: 私は本を読む人は田中さんです。
commonMistakes.right: 本を読んでいる人は田中さんです。
commonMistakes.why: は marks the topic of the whole sentence, so it is not used inside a describing clause. Keep one clear topic.

usageNotes: は also carries contrast (example 3). Old information / what you are talking about takes は; new or emphasised information takes が.
jlptTips: If the sentence starts with a person, thing or time and then describes it, the first particle is は. If the word before the blank is a question word (誰・何・どこ), it is が.
Watch for contrast sentences with が or けど in the middle: 〜は〜ですが、〜は〜. Both blanks take は.
